candidate_relations.reason: There is no clinical or electrical myotonia to support myotonic dystrophy.
Acid alpha-glucosidase activity was normal, excluding Pompe disease.
Facioscapulohumeral dystrophy has a different regional pattern than this congenital-onset SCN4A myopathy.
Muscular dystrophy is a broad parent and does not identify SCN4A congenital myopathy.
Becker muscular dystrophy is an XP21 dystrophinopathy, incompatible with this female congenital myopathy.
Bethlem myopathy is collagen-VI related with contractures not established as the gene diagnosis.
Collagen VI-related myopathy is a different genetic myopathy.
Congenital disorder is a nonspecific parent.
Congenital muscular dystrophy implies a dystrophic biopsy/gene class rather than SCN4A congenital myopathy.
Rigid spine muscular dystrophy (SEPN1/etc.) is a different congenital myopathy/dystrophy.
Duchenne muscular dystrophy is incompatible with an affected female and this biopsy.
Ullrich congenital muscular dystrophy is collagen-VI disease, not SCN4A.
Myotonic dystrophy type 1 is unsupported without myotonia.
Myopathy is the correct family but omits SCN4A and the specified variants.
Nerve conductions were normal; spinal muscular atrophy is a motor-neuron disease, not this myopathy (despite some neuropathic EMG features).
Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy is a different genetic dystrophy class.
Internalized nuclei can suggest centronuclear myopathy as a histologic pattern, not the SCN4A gene diagnosis.
Nemaline rods are not described on the biopsy.
Neuropathy conflicts with the reference congenital myopathy despite some neuropathic EMG motor-unit changes.

case_quality_flags: Reference specifies SCN4A compound-heterozygous congenital myopathy; no candidate names SCN4A or those variants.
